name: Familial Cutaneous Telangiectasia and Oropharyngeal Cancer Predisposition Syndrome
aliases: Familial Cutaneous Telangiectasia with Oropharyngeal Carcinoma Risk
Inherited Cutaneous Telangiectasia and Oropharyngeal Cancer Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Cutaneous Telangiectasia and Oropharyngeal Cancer Predisposition Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple cutaneous telangiectasias predominantly on the face, lips, and oral mucosa
First-degree relative with documented oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma or cutaneous telangiectasia
Histologically confirmed oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Telangiectasia involving oropharyngeal mucosa detected by clinical examination
Exclusion of other hereditary telangiectasia syndromes such as hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cutaneous telangiectasia and a positive family history of oropharyngeal cancer or telangiectasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not yet standardized.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple facial and oral mucosal telangiectasias
pathognomonic.notes: Telangiectasias are small dilated blood vessels visible on the skin and mucosa.
searchTerms: small red spots on face and mouth lining
visible tiny blood vessels on lips and cheeks
clusters of dilated blood vessels in mouth and face

pathognomonic.symptomName: Familial clustering of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
pathognomonic.notes: Strong familial predisposition to oropharyngeal cancer.
searchTerms: family history of throat cancers
multiple relatives with mouth and throat tumors
inherited clustering of throat cancer cases

common.symptomName: Recurrent epistaxis due to nasal mucosal telangiectasia
common.notes: Nosebleeds caused by fragile telangiectatic vessels.
searchTerms: frequent nosebleeds from nasal blood vessels
repeated bleeding from nose due to vessel abnormalities
nosebleeds caused by fragile nasal vessels

common.notes: May precede or accompany cancer development.
searchTerms: persistent sore throat or mouth ulcers
chronic discomfort in throat area
long-lasting mouth or throat pain
red skin patches that turn white when pressed
blanching redness around small blood vessels
skin redness that fades with pressure near telangiectasias

common.symptomName: Mild anemia secondary to recurrent mucosal bleeding
common.notes: Due to chronic blood loss from fragile vessels.
searchTerms: mild low red blood cell count from bleeding
slight anemia due to repeated mucosal blood loss
chronic mild anemia from bleeding sites

occasional.notes: Difficulty swallowing due to mucosal involvement.
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to throat lesions
painful swallowing from mouth or throat sores
swallowing problems related to oropharyngeal damage

occasional.notes: May result from tumor involvement or mucosal irritation.
searchTerms: hoarse voice
voice changes
loss of normal voice

occasional.notes: Visible dilated vessels on the eye surface.
searchTerms: small red blood vessels on eye surface
visible tiny vessels on conjunctiva
red spots on the white part of the eye

occasional.symptomName: Mild fatigue related to chronic anemia
searchTerms: mild tiredness from ongoing anemia
feeling slightly fatigued due to low blood count
chronic low energy related to anemia
lung blood vessel malformations
pulmonary AV malformations
abnormal lung blood flow
hidden bleeding in digestive tract from blood vessels
gastrointestinal bleeding causing anemia
blood loss inside stomach or intestines from vessel abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to paradoxical embolism
rare.notes: Due to right-to-left shunting from vascular malformations.
searchTerms: brain or nerve problems from abnormal blood clots
neurological symptoms caused by embolism
nerve damage due to paradoxical blood clots

laboratory: Mild microcytic anemia due to chronic mucosal bleeding
imaging: MRI or CT scan showing oropharyngeal mass consistent with squamous cell carcinoma
Contrast echocardiography or CT angiography to detect pulmonary arteriovenous malformations
other: Histopathology confirming squamous cell carcinoma in oropharyngeal lesions

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of visceral arteriovenous malformations more common
Genetic mutations in ENG, ACVRL1, or SMAD4 genes
Predominant predisposition to oral cavity cancers without vascular lesions

redFlags: Family history of early-onset oropharyngeal cancer
